description: Palettes derived from golden ratio subdivisions and proportions

math_basis.note: Golden ratio φ = (1+√5)/2. Golden angle = 360°/φ² = 360°×(2-φ). All golden proportions are self-similar under φ scaling.

palettes.name: Golden Triad
palettes.description: Three colors at golden-angle intervals starting from 0°
palettes.aesthetic_notes: Three maximally spread hues. Red-teal-violet. More interesting than primary triadic, less predictable.

palettes.name: Golden Pentatonic
palettes.description: Five golden-angle hues. Perfect for 5-element systems.
palettes.aesthetic_notes: Five spread hues covering warm, cool, and neutral territory evenly.

palettes.name: Golden Gradient Warm
palettes.description: 8 golden-angle hues with decreasing saturation — creates a warm gradient effect
palettes.aesthetic_notes: Saturation decreases as hue spreads. Starts vivid, relaxes into muted tones. φ-proportioned saturation steps.

palettes.name: Golden Dark 10
palettes.description: 10 golden-angle hues at dark, rich values — for dark themes and generative backgrounds
palettes.aesthetic_notes: Rich, jewel-tone palette. No two colors are similar. Works as a 10-color categorical palette for dark-mode data visualization.
